subject: Orpheus AI — platform fit and integration next steps

Subject: Orpheus AI — platform fit and integration next steps

Thanks again for a productive demo earlier today — really appreciated the candidness on latency targets and the data residency constraints. I wanted to capture the core takeaways and suggested next steps so we have a single place to iterate from.

Recap of pain points you described
- High-rate low-latency inference for user-facing summarization (p95 < 400ms for 256-token requests).
- Need for on-prem/VPC deployment for regulated customers in the EU (audit logs, KMS integration).
- Current cost per active user is too high on your in-house infra; you’re evaluating batching/quantization to bring down unit cost.

Proposed Redwood fit (high level)
- Dedicated/private deployment: VPC deployment with KMS/HSM support for key management and audit log integration.
- Serving capabilities: streaming token responses + function-call hooks for structured output (we can return JSON object schemas rather than freeform text).
- Cost controls: batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce token counts on repeated prompts; recommend INT8-quantized variant for bulk inference.
- Embeddings + reranking: hybrid approach where you host embeddings locally and use Redwood’s rerank endpoint to keep rerank latency under 150ms for top-10.

Technical asks / open questions (for Karthik & Orpheus engineering)
1) Typical request size distribution and percent of streaming vs complete-response workflows?
2) Any model architecture constraints (we discussed Llama-3 variants, confirm if you can accept quantized variants).
3) Data retention window for KV caches and audit log retention requirement (30/90/365 days).

Immediate next steps
- Karthik: I’ve asked him to follow up with a short tech note on the functions-calling approach + SDK changes needed (see his draft below). Target EOD Wed (3/24).
- Rishi/Monica: Share SOW draft + security snapshot for internal review (attached).
- Leah/Tom: Confirm procurement timeline and any mandatory clauses (export control, data locality).

Attachments referenced

- redwood-inference-arch.png (attached)
- security-summary-snapshot.pdf (attached)

Thanks — happy to hop on another call if helpful.

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful and captures the conversation well. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Request distribution: roughly 60% short summarization (<= 128 tokens), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512). Streaming is used for the short/medium flows to improve perceived latency.
- Models: we prefer Llama-3 family but need confirmation that quantized INT8 preserves function-call outputs and rerank accuracy.
- Data retention: for now 90 days for logs and 30 days for KV cache.

Procurement note: procurement@orpheus.ai will need a redlined SOW and an initial cost estimate by 3/31 to include in our Q2 budget approval. Also, security will require a SOC2 snapshot and an explanation of key rotation cadence.

If Karthik can outline the SDK changes (function-calling vs structured-output), that will help our eng team plan. Can we target a technical sync Wed 3/24 at 10:00am CET?

Leah / team — quick tech note as promised. High level items for your eng team to vet: 

1) SDK changes & function calling - Redwood SDK will expose a function-calling layer that maps to typed schema outputs (JSON Schema / protobuf). That means your app can register expected output shapes and Redwood will surface structured responses plus a confidence score. No major protocol changes — just additional headers and a JSON contract on the call.

2) Streaming + structured output - We support streaming of structured tokens. For your short/medium summarization use case we recommend streaming envelope frames that include "partial_object" tokens — consumers reconstruct the JSON as frames arrive. This keeps perceived latency low while delivering valid JSON incrementally.

3) Embeddings & rerank flow - Indexed locally (you can keep your embeddings service on-prem). For rerank we provide a compact rerank endpoint that accepts top-K candidates and returns a sorted list with scores. Rerank latency target for top-10 on dedicated infra is ~120-150ms.

4) Quantization tradeoffs - INT8 preserves most semantic fidelity but affects floating-point calibrations used in rerank scoring. We'll run a short A/B in your sandbox (5k queries) to verify rerank delta before we commit to INT8 in production.

5) Security & logs - We'll provide KMS integration notes and audit log export (JSON lines) to your S3-like endpoint. Key rotation cadence is configurable; default 90 days — we can tighten per policy.

Let me know if you'd like the dev checklist as a Markdown doc — I can post to the Drive link Rishi provided. Happy to take the technical sync Wed 3/24 at 10:00am CET.
